imagesViewedThisTurn.reviewScope: Hands making an explanatory card with two pictures, paint and brush; caption describes communication and does not claim every watercolor mixture is a true solution.
First two liquid levels are similar and third is higher; all are clear. Current caption requires numeric practice data and does not infer concentration from color.

Comparable tomatoes: left fully submerged away from bottom, middle slightly emerges and right emerges farther. Still image alone is not a motion/time record; current text supplies controlled comparison conditions.
Both balances carry a beaker and paper; paper contains powder before and is empty after. Displays are blank; caption separates the 139 g practice calculation from the picture.
Powder and two clear liquids correspond to assigned solute/solvent/solution roles. Image itself does not identify chemical composition or measured quantity.
White solid visibly remains at left bottom; none is visible at right. Current captions match the displayed contrast.
Probes are submerged above the bottoms; white solid remains only at left. Temperature values come from supplied conditions/measurement, not visible displays.
Dark colored liquid and color spreading are visible. Caption describes water-based ink observation without reading numerical concentration from the still image.
Original illustration compares the same beaker/paper/sugar using a balance before and after dissolving. Caption already distinguishes this example from the numerical practice example.
Visible 설탕(용질), 물(용매), 설탕물(용액), 용해 labels agree with the roles. Original depiction is retained.
